title: KV prefetch race experiment log
content:
Context:
Quick scratchpad for the weird token-loss / decoder divergence we've been seeing on long context replays when prefetch is enabled. Suspect a prefetch -> kv-index race that interacts with the kernel selector (fast_small_attn vs fallback_dense) when sequence length crosses a threshold mid-request.

Observed symptoms (short):
- When streaming long conversations (seqlen ~ 12k tokens) with KV prefetch turned on, some requests show missing early prefix tokens in the generated output (leading to coherence drop).
- Issue appears intermittently and correlates with a frequency of kernel switch log entries ("selected_kernel=fallback_dense" vs "selected_kernel=fast_small_attn") around the same request id.
- Replays under deterministic single-threaded env do NOT reproduce reliably; more common on high-concurrency machines.

Hypothesis summary (working):
1) Prefetch writes kv-index entries into per-session index concurrently while attention kernel selection reads sequence-length distribution to choose kernel. If prefetch finishes slightly after selector reads, the selector may think seqlen is below the fast kernel threshold and picks fast_small_attn, but the KV layout is partially updated -> mismatch in kv offset expectations -> keys get looked up wrong (shift by one shard) -> lost earlier prefix.
2) Alternatively, the kernel selector re-evaluates mid-run when KV batch grows (we have a soft re-check at layer N). If re-evaluation doesn't rebind the KV base pointer, the attention compute uses the wrong cache base on later layers.

Repro attempts and commands (notes):
- Baseline run (no prefetch):
  export PREFETCH_ENABLED=false
  ./tools/infer_runner --model rwlm-7b --input-file tests/long_convo.json --concurrency 16 --max-seq 13000 --log-level debug 
  -> no anomalies across 1000 requests.

- With prefetch ON:
  export PREFETCH_ENABLED=true
  ./tools/infer_runner --model rwlm-7b --input-file tests/long_convo.json --concurrency 16 --max-seq 13000 --log-level debug 
  -> ~1.8% of requests show missing prefix tokens.

- Capture verbose logs for a suspicious request id (req=20250312-7):
  [2026-03-09T15:43:21.271Z] req=20250312-7 start session_id=sess-53a
  [2026-03-09T15:43:21.272Z] prefetch: enqueued prefetch job (job=pf-918) for kvrange=[0..8191]
  [2026-03-09T15:43:21.275Z] kv-index: append index epoch=12 offset=65536 session=sess-53a
  [2026-03-09T15:43:21.276Z] selector: sample_seqlen_distribution mean=11000 p90=12400 -> selected_kernel=fast_small_attn
  [2026-03-09T15:43:21.279Z] prefetch: completed pf-918 commit_offset=65536
  [2026-03-09T15:43:21.280Z] layer=0 execute using kernel=fast_small_attn kv_base=0 expected_kv_base=65536
  [2026-03-09T15:43:21.281Z] ERROR: attn_lookup_mismatch session=sess-53a layer=0 key_idx=3 looked_up_token_hash=0x0 expected_hash=0x9ab4

- Note: Looked_up_token_hash=0x0 happens when kv read returns empty slot (possible off-by-one in base offset).

Short Python reproducer (local single-thread):
  # minimal reproducer pseudo-code
  session = Session()
  # kick prefetch in background thread
  spawn(prefetch_kv, session, target_range)
  # selector reads metadata to choose kernel
  chosen = kernel_selector.choose(session.metadata)
  # if chosen==fast_small_attn and prefetch not committed yet -> mismatch

Things I tried and results:
- Forced barrier after prefetch commit (synchronous commit): eliminates the bug entirely in stress runs (n=10k).
- Added an atomic publish flag (kv_index.committed = True before append visible): reduces occurrence but doesn't eliminate (race window shifted).
- Increased selector re-check frequency (re-query metadata before each layer): reduced but not 0; expensive CPU wise.
- Disabled kernel fallback entirely (force dense for long requests): removes mismatch but cost regresses 1.7x.

Signals to capture next (metrics/logs to add):
- Add 'kv_publish_version' to selector input logs so we can correlate which version selector saw vs commit version.
- Emit event when kernel rebind happens: "kernel_rebind session=.. from X to Y at layer L" with timestamps.
- Track per-layer kv_base pointer in logs.

Small patch idea (non-invasive):
- Maintain an epoch counter (kv_epoch) that increments on any KV structural update. Selector reads kv_epoch and includes it in the kernel binding. At exec time, validate epoch hasn't changed; if changed, rebind or fail fast with clear telemetry. This is a lightweight guard and can be toggled by config.

Alternate approach (more surgical):
- Ensure prefetch commit uses a single atomic update of the per-session kv_base (CAS). Selector binds to the atomic value and kernel exec reads same atomic. If CAS semantics hold, the mismatch should vanish. But must verify memory model across replicas (numa, gpu host).

Short list of follow-ups / experiments to run:
- EXP-A: Run with PREFETCH_SYNC=true for 24h on canary cluster and measure regressions (already partial run for 4h looks clean).
- EXP-B: Instrument selector with kv_epoch logging, run with prefetch stress 100k requests to get correlation matrix (kernel_choice vs epoch mismatch).
- EXP-C: Introduce a cheap layer-0 sanity check in attention lookup: verify token hashes for first N keys; if mismatch, increment a metric and fallback to safe kernel. This might be an acceptable safety net until a proper fix lands.

Notes / gotchas:
- Reproducer is timing-sensitive; heavy concurrency and multi-session prefetch queuing increases chance. Single-thread repro is unreliable.
- GPUs with different memory allocators (NVIDIA A100 vs H100) showed slightly different race frequency — suggests dependency on host-side allocator timing and copy latency.
- There's a historical PR that changed 'selector sampling window' (PR #601) — might be related. See linked PR above.

Open questions for Diego/infra:
- Are there any guarantees about ordering of prefetch completion vs index append visibility? Is the append exposed to other threads before prefetch buffer is fully materialized?
- When kernel_selector samples distribution, is it permissible for it to assume kv layout is immutable for the duration of a request?

Immediate next steps (my plan):
1) Add kv_epoch logging to selector and prefetch commit (small patch).
2) Run EXP-B overnight with expanded logs and collect sample of mismatch traces (req ids).
3) If epoch mismatches correlate with errors, prepare minimal CAS publish patch and run canary.
4) Draft a short postmortem-style note if we see customer-facing incidents (include mitigation: PREFETCH_SYNC toggle).

Todo (quick):
- [ ] Implement kv_epoch logging (Asha)
- [ ] Run EXP-B job and collect data (Priya)
- [ ] Prototype CAS publish (Diego)
- [ ] Prepare config toggle and doc for ops (Asha)

Misc scratch ideas:
- Could we move kernel selection to be decided per-layer using only stable per-layer metadata (layer-aware kv window) so mid-request structural updates are naturally isolated? Tradeoff: additional selector calls.
- Instrument a "canary kernel" that runs shadow attention compute on first layer comparing outputs of both kernels (cheap hash compare) to detect mismatch early without full fallback.

Endnotes: this doc is a working scratchpad — will tidy up after EXP-B. Keep using PREFETCH_SYNC toggle when running customer-like loads until fix verified.

-- Asha
